methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series G → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.25x) to $150M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 1 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 11 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Distalmotion, a Series G robotics and manufacturing company founded by Michael Friedrich, has raised $150M+ to date. The valuation universe comprises 9 private peers (including Divergent, Exotec, and Locus Robotics) and 1 public comparable, though none yield a sufficiently dense peer set for robust median-based triangulation at the Series G stage.

Given data constraints, stage-progression analysis provides the primary valuation anchor. Using total raised ($150M) as a proxy base value and applying a typical 1.25x step-up multiplier for Series G advancement yields an implied valuation of $188M. This method assumes capital deployment has been reasonably efficient and that subsequent-stage entry multiples hold for this cohort.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $159M (low) to $216M (median), with $188M as the central point estimate. The range reflects standard stage-progression variance rather than triangulation across multiple methods. Key uncertainties include the absence of contemporaneous Series G robotics comps at similar valuation tiers, which limits confidence in the multiplier assumption, and limited visibility into Distalmotion's unit economics, revenue trajectory, or capital deployment efficiency relative to peers. A narrower range would require additional peer data or portfolio company financials at comparable stages.
